chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say:
A Jew, a Christian, and a Magian may have retaliation enforced among themselves, and some of them are killed for others, when they kill intentionally.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيُّ: a Christian, as one party subject to this ruling
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيُّ: a Magian, as one party subject to this ruling
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيُّ: a Jew, as one party subject to this ruling
key_terms.يَقْتَصُّ: retaliation is exacted; legal retribution is carried out

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about qisas between Jews, Christians, and Magians in cases of intentional murder?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning qisas among non-Muslim protected communities, specifically Jews, Christians, and Magians. It indicates that retaliatory punishment and execution apply between them in cases of intentional killing.
